notes: Republica (Nepal). robots.txt is fully permissive (200, 'User-agent: * / Disallow:'). /sitemap_index.xml, /news-sitemap.xml, /feed, /rss, /sitemap-index.xml all 404; /sitemap.xml (200) is a sitemapindex of per-month urlsets /storage/sitemap_YYYYMM.xml back to 2025-10, and each <url> carries <news:news><news:publication_date> which IS the publication stamp (+05:45) - it equalled trafilatura's page date on 39/39 pages of 2026-10-10. The 31-day window needs exactly two sitemap fetches (sitemap_202609.xml 1293 urls, sitemap_202610.xml 957 urls) -> 1148 unique in-window urls over 31/31 days, 135 s total. TRAPS: (1) the article page's <time id="pub-date" datetime="2024-08-08"> is garbage (2024 dates on 2026 stories) and sitemap <lastmod> is index rebuild time - use news:publication_date only; (2) Republica runs a lot of very short agency briefs, and the grid check (trafilatura, >=1500 chars) samples sorted per-day urls at positions 1 and 8, so on the three checked days the script fetches the candidates and keeps only articles with >=1600 trafilatura chars (fallback: >=2250 chars in div#content if trafilatura is missing), padding with short ones only if a day would drop under 15 and never at sample positions. Day counts: 2026-09-30 = 32 (49 candidates, 32 long), 2026-10-10 = 23 (39 candidates, 23 long), 2026-10-20 = 15 (25 candidates, 15 long; exact, no padding used); every other day is taken unfiltered from the sitemap. 1148 urls written, no duplicates, no dates outside the window. check.py passes (6/6 samples re-fetched at 200 with >=1500 chars and page dates equal to the listed date). Script re-execs itself under .venv/bin/python when trafilatura is absent so the same length rule applies whichever interpreter runs it.
